Finally, with the iron_axe (or more precisely, a pickaxe-level tool that the iron_axe's crafting station area also provides), the player must mine light_blue_glazed_terracotta. However, let me reconsider the dependency: an iron_axe isn't the right tool for mining glazed terracotta (you need a pickaxe). Let me restructure: The blue_concrete serves as a landmark guiding the player to a crafting area. The iron_axe craft requires finding the crafting table and materials (near the blue_concrete). The light_blue_glazed_terracotta mining requires a pickaxe which will be available in the same supply chest - but the terracotta block is located past/near the blue_concrete landmark. Actually, let me design a cleaner dependency: (1) find blue_concrete - this is a landmark near the supplies, (2) craft to iron_axe - using materials found near the blue_concrete, (3) mine light_blue_glazed_terracotta - the iron_axe can technically break glazed terracotta (any tool works, but it's fastest with a pickaxe; without any tool it's very slow). The iron_axe will allow the player to break the terracotta block (it just won't be as fast as a pickaxe, but it will still drop the item). Wait - glazed terracotta requires a pickaxe to drop itself. Without a pickaxe, it drops nothing. So iron_axe won't work for mining terracotta. Let me revise: I'll place a pickaxe in the chest as well, but make the dependency that the player needs to first find the area (blue_concrete) to access supplies, then craft the iron_axe as a separate task, and mine the terracotta requires finding it near the blue_concrete. Actually, let me simplify the dependency structure: find blue_concrete leads to the area with both the crafting supplies AND the terracotta block. The crafting table there enables crafting the iron_axe. The terracotta is nearby and a pickaxe will be in the supply chest. So: find blue_concrete → craft iron_axe (materials and crafting table near blue_concrete), and find blue_concrete → mine light_blue_glazed_terracotta (the block is placed near the blue_concrete, and a pickaxe is in the chest there).

Uses inventory_has because the mined light_blue_glazed_terracotta block drop ends up in the player's inventory. This rule also implicitly validates correct tool usage: glazed terracotta only drops as an item when mined with a pickaxe (the iron_pickaxe from the chest). Using any other tool (including the iron_axe) or bare hands destroys the block without dropping it. No light_blue_glazed_terracotta item exists in the starting inventory, so presence confirms successful mining with the correct tool.
